name: wirouter_keyrec
desc: Recover the default WPA passphrases from supported routers
why: Recovers default WPA passphrases from router firmware weaknesses, a sharp look at how default credentials are derived.

brief.what_it_is: WiRouter KeyRec is a platform-independent tool, version 1.1.2 per the homepage, that recovers the default WPA passphrases of a fixed list of router models. The homepage names Telecom Italia Alice AGPF, Fastweb Pirelli, Fastweb Tesley, Eircom Netopia, and Pirelli TeleTu/Tele 2. The page does not say what the tool takes as input or what exact output format it produces. The package metadata lists two executables, wirouterkeyrec and wr_iwlist.sh, but the homepage does not describe either one.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no stated motivation beyond describing the tool's function. It notes that the software was once used by the Italian Carabinieri.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the mechanism. The scout note's phrase about firmware weaknesses is not supported by anything on this page, so it should not be repeated as fact without checking the source code or documentation.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no installation steps, dependencies, or first-run instructions. The package metadata says a Homebrew formula exists with the executables wirouterkeyrec and wr_iwlist.sh. No README or repository was reachable from the homepage.
brief.standout: It is a small, old, single-purpose tool that targets specific ISP-supplied router firmware and their default-passphrase schemes, which makes it a concrete case of default credentials being derivable. The page also records a law-enforcement user, which is unusual for a security tool.
brief.status: Quiet. The tool's last update is listed as 12-2012 on the homepage. The page also shows a 2014 CV and a 2010 paper, so the site itself appears to have little recent activity. No later release or commit was visible.
brief.caveats: The homepage lists only older Italian ISP router models, so the tool is unlikely to work on current hardware. Its use is for recovering keys on routers, and the page does not discuss authorization or legal limits. Recovering a passphrase from a router you do not own or administer is unauthorized access. The page does not state a license, and the install and usage details are missing. The package metadata has an empty caveats field.
quotes: WiRouter KeyRec is a powerful and platform independent software to recover the default WPA passphrases of the supported router models
In the past, this software was also used by the italian Carabinieri.
fetch_log: https://www.salvatorefresta.net/tools/ - fetched OK. Describes WiRouter KeyRec v1.1.2 in a short paragraph. No README, docs, download page, or source link was present in the returned text, so no further fetches were made.
